T H E C A S E F O R T O D A Y · B R I V A N E I S A F I C T I O N A L C OM P A N Y

Brivane paid for four years of work, and a former 
engineer now sells a copy

What happened
Brivane is a small company that makes acoustic sensors. Brivane 
spent four years and most of its money perfecting one sensor. 
The work produced design drawings, test data and a calibration 
process that the team calls “the recipe”. Brivane never applied for 
a patent, a legal right over an invention that a government office 
grants. Brivane kept every file on a shared drive that every 
employee could open.

What happened next
Aiko Tanaka was Brivane's best engineer. Aiko resigned in the 
spring. Her employment contract said nothing about what she 
could do after leaving. Four months later, Aiko's new company 
launched a sensor called Sonaris. Sonaris is almost identical to 
Brivane's sensor and sells for two-thirds of the price.

Aiko's lawyer says
“Everything Aiko built lives in Aiko's head. Brivane applied for no 
patent and locked nothing away. Copying something that 
nobody protected is competition, not theft.”

Brivane's lawyer says
“Brivane paid for every hour in which that sensor was invented. If 
paid work can walk out of the door on a Friday, no company will 
pay for the first year.”

QU ES TIO N
The two lawyers agree on every fact. What exactly are the two lawyers disagreeing about?

segments.en: T H E C A S E F O R T O D A Y · B R I V A N E I S A F I C T I O N A L C OM P A N Y

segments.en: Brivane paid for four years of work, and a former engineer now sells a copy

segments.en: What happened Brivane is a small company that makes acoustic sensors. Brivane spent four years and most of its money perfecting one sensor. The work produced design drawings, test data and a calibration process that the team calls “the recipe”. Brivane never applied for a patent, a legal right over an invention that a government office grants. Brivane kept every file on a shared drive that every employee could open.
segments.zh:
发生了什么 Brivane 是一家生产声学传感器的小公司。Brivane 花了四年时间和大部分资金来完善一款传感器。这项工作产生了设计图纸、测试数据和校准过程，团队称之为“配方”。布里瓦恩从未申请过专利，这是政府办公室授予的一项发明的合法权利。

Brivane 将每个文件保存在每个员工都可以打开的共享驱动器上。
segments.explain: 这里的 patent（专利）指：公开技术方案后，由国家在有限期限内授予的排他保护。

segments.en: What happened next Aiko Tanaka was Brivane's best engineer. Aiko resigned in the spring. Her employment contract said nothing about what she could do after leaving. Four months later, Aiko's new company launched a sensor called Sonaris. Sonaris is almost identical to Brivane's sensor and sells for two-thirds of the price.
segments.zh:
接下来发生的事情 Aiko Tanaka 是 Brivane 最好的工程师。爱子于春天辞职。她的雇佣合同没有提及她离开后可以做什么。四个月后，Aiko 的新公司推出了一款名为 Sonaris 的传感器。

Sonaris 与 Brivane 的传感器几乎相同，售价仅为 Brivane 的三分之二。

segments.en: Aiko's lawyer says “Everything Aiko built lives in Aiko's head. Brivane applied for no patent and locked nothing away. Copying something that nobody protected is competition, not theft.”
segments.zh: Aiko 的律师表示，“Aiko 构建的一切都存在于 Aiko 的脑海中。Brivane 没有申请专利，也没有锁定任何东西。复制没有人保护的东西是竞争，而不是盗窃。”
segments.explain: 这里的 patent（专利）指：公开技术方案后，由国家在有限期限内授予的排他保护。

segments.en: Brivane's lawyer says “Brivane paid for every hour in which that sensor was invented. If paid work can walk out of the door on a Friday, no company will pay for the first year.”
segments.zh: Brivane 的律师表示，“Brivane 为发明该传感器的每一小时付费。如果带薪工作可以在周五走出大门，那么没有公司会支付第一年的费用。”

segments.zh: 问题 两位律师在所有事实上都达成一致。两位律师究竟在什么问题上存在分歧？

pages.english:
I N TH E N E W S · T H E F I VE A RT I C L E S Y O U RE A D

Five real disputes.
The court never ask who worked the hardest

Trade secret · Rippling v Deel · March 
2025
A trade secret is valuable information 
that a company keeps secret on 
purpose. Rippling sued its rival Deel in 
California. Rippling says an employee 
passed Rippling's sales information to 
Deel. Rippling caught the employee with 
a fake Slack channel.

Trade mark · Thatchers v Aldi · January 
2025
A trade mark is a registered sign that 
tells buyers who made the goods. 
Thatchers registered the look of its lemon 
cider can. The Court of Appeal ruled that 
Aldi's similar can took unfair advantage 
of that mark: Aldi profited from the 
reputation that Thatchers had built.

Copyright · Ed Sheeran · November 2024

Copyright protects original music, text, 
images and code from copying. A 
company holding part of the rights in 
Marvin Gaye's “Let's Get It On” sued Ed 
Sheeran. The appeals court ruled that a 
common chord progression belongs to 
nobody.

Patent · Masimo v US Customs · August 
2025
A US trade court banned imports of some 
Apple watches in 2023, because the 
watches used Masimo's patented 
technology. Apple moved one 
calculation to the iPhone. US Customs 
then let the watches in, and Masimo sued 
US Customs.

Trade mark · Iceland v Iceland · July 
2025
Iceland Foods, a UK supermarket, held 
the EU trade mark “Iceland”. The country 
of Iceland challenged the mark. The EU 
General Court cancelled the mark, 
because a country's name tells buyers 
where goods come from.

What the five have in common
In every dispute, each company held 
exactly what its registrations and 
contracts gave it. Hard work alone gave 
each company nothing.

segments.en: Copyright · Ed Sheeran · November 2024

segments.en: Copyright protects original music, text, images and code from copying. A company holding part of the rights in Marvin Gaye's “Let's Get It On” sued Ed Sheeran. The appeals court ruled that a common chord progression belongs to nobody.
segments.zh: 版权保护原创音乐、文本、图像和代码免遭复制。一家拥有马文·盖伊 (Marvin Gaye) 的《Let's Get It On》部分版权的公司起诉艾德·希兰 (Ed Sheeran)。上诉法院裁定，共同的和弦进行不属于任何人。
segments.explain: 这里的 copyright（版权）指：保护原创作品的具体表达，通常不需要登记才能产生。

segments.en: Patent · Masimo v US Customs · August 2025 A US trade court banned imports of some Apple watches in 2023, because the watches used Masimo's patented technology. Apple moved one calculation to the iPhone. US Customs then let the watches in, and Masimo sued US Customs.
segments.zh: 专利 · Masimo 诉美国海关 · 2025 年 8 月 美国贸易法庭于 2023 年禁止进口部分苹果手表，因为这些手表使用了 Masimo 的专利技术。苹果将​​一项计算转移到了 iPhone 上。美国海关随后将手表放了进来，马西莫起诉了美国海关。
segments.explain: 这里的 patent（专利）指：公开技术方案后，由国家在有限期限内授予的排他保护。

segments.en: Trade mark · Iceland v Iceland · July 2025 Iceland Foods, a UK supermarket, held the EU trade mark “Iceland”. The country of Iceland challenged the mark. The EU General Court cancelled the mark, because a country's name tells buyers where goods come from.
segments.zh: 商标·冰岛诉冰岛·2025年7月英国超市冰岛食品公司持有欧盟商标“Iceland”。冰岛国家挑战了这个目标。欧盟普通法院取消了该标志，因为一个国家的名称告诉买家商品来自哪里。

segments.en: What the five have in common In every dispute, each company held exactly what its registrations and contracts gave it. Hard work alone gave each company nothing.
segments.zh: 五家公司的共同点 在每一次纠纷中，每家公司都准确地掌握了其注册和合同所赋予的内容。单靠努力工作对每个公司来说一无所获。

pages.english:
P A R T 1 · C O N C E P T
An IP right lets its owner stop other people, for a limited 
time, in one country

An intellectual property right (IP right) is a legal ownership right over a creation. 
The law of one country grants the power. The owner uses the power to stop other people copying, making, selling or using the creation.

WHO

Everyone except the owner of 
the IP right

OWE S WHAT

must not copy, make, sell or 
use the protected creation 
without permission

TO WHOM

the owner, in the country that 
granted the right

I F N OT

The owner can ask a court to 
stop the copying and to award 
money.

Three limits on every IP right
The right ends after a fixed time: a patent lasts about 20 years. 
The right covers only what the law defines. The right exists only in 
the country that granted it.

What an IP right does not do
Nobody owns an idea. No government watches for copying on 
the owner's behalf. If the owner does nothing, nothing happens.

Example · Masimo and Apple
In 2023 the US International Trade Commission ruled that some 
Apple watches used Masimo's patented technology. The 
Commission banned imports of those watches.

What goes wrong without this rule
A company that believes it owns everything it built sues on a right 
that does not exist, and loses.

segments.en: An intellectual property right (IP right) is a legal ownership right over a creation. The law of one country grants the power. The owner uses the power to stop other people copying, making, selling or using the creation.
segments.zh: 知识产权（IP 权）是对创作物的合法所有权。一国法律授予权力。所有者有权阻止其他人复制、制作、销售或使用该创作。
segments.explain: 这里的 intellectual property（知识产权）指：法律对技术、作品、标志等无形成果给出的特定排他权。

segments.en: must not copy, make, sell or use the protected creation without permission
segments.zh: 未经许可不得复制、制作、出售或使用受保护的创作

segments.en: TO WHOM
segments.zh: 向谁承担

segments.en: the owner, in the country that granted the right

segments.en: I F N OT
segments.zh: 如果没有

segments.en: The owner can ask a court to stop the copying and to award money.
segments.zh: 所有者可以要求法院停止复制并判给金钱。

segments.en: Three limits on every IP right The right ends after a fixed time: a patent lasts about 20 years. The right covers only what the law defines. The right exists only in the country that granted it.
segments.zh: 每个知识产权的三个限制 权利在固定期限后终止：专利的有效期约为 20 年。该权利仅涵盖法律定义的内容。该权利仅存在于授予该权利的国家。
segments.explain: 这里的 patent（专利）指：公开技术方案后，由国家在有限期限内授予的排他保护。

segments.en: What an IP right does not do Nobody owns an idea. No government watches for copying on the owner's behalf. If the owner does nothing, nothing happens.
segments.zh: 知识产权不能做什么 没有人拥有想法。没有政府代表所有者监视复制行为。如果所有者什么都不做，就不会发生任何事情。

P A R T 1 · C O N C E P T

The IP bargain: society grants a monopoly, and the 
creator gives society the creation

A monopoly is the power to be the only seller of something. Society grants the creator a monopoly for a limited time. In return, the creator 
gives society the creation. A patent owner must also publish how the invention works. Lawyers call this exchange the IP bargain.

Example · Grenat Batteries (fictional)
Grenat patented its battery electrolyte in three countries. The law 
required Grenat to publish the recipe. A rival read the patent and 
changed one ingredient. The rival now sells a competing battery 
legally. Grenat's patent worked as the law intends.

Example · Kaze Energy (fictional)
Kaze chose not to apply for a patent on its pellet recipe. Kaze 
never had to publish the recipe. In return, Kaze had to guard the 
recipe every day. The law gives Kaze nothing against a rival who 
works out the recipe alone.

What goes wrong without this rule
A founder cannot have a patent and total secrecy together. A 
patent application publishes the invention. A secret stays 
protected only while the founder publishes nothing.

segments.en: A trade mark protects the sign that tells buyers who made the goods, not the goods themselves
segments.zh: 商标保护的是告诉买家谁制造了商品的标志，而不是商品本身
segments.explain: 这里的 trade mark（商标）指：帮助消费者识别商品或服务来源的标志。

segments.en: A business registers a sign as its trade mark: a word, a logo, a colour or a package design. A registry refuses a sign that only describes the goods or where the goods come from. A court asks whether ordinary buyers are likely to mix up two signs. Lawyers call this test the likelihood of confusion.
segments.zh: 企业将标志注册为其商标：文字、徽标、颜色或包装设计。登记处拒绝仅描述货物或货物来源的标志。法院询问普通买家是否可能混淆两个标志。律师称此测试为混淆可能性。
segments.explain: 这里的 trade mark（商标）指：帮助消费者识别商品或服务来源的标志。

segments.en: Example · Iceland v Iceland Iceland Foods applied for the EU trade mark “Iceland” in 2013. The country of Iceland challenged the mark in 2018. On 16 July 2025 the EU General Court cancelled the mark. The court said that shoppers could believe the frozen food came from Iceland.
segments.zh: 示例 · 冰岛诉冰岛 冰岛食品公司于 2013 年申请了欧盟商标“Iceland”。冰岛国家于 2018 年对该商标提出质疑。2025 年 7 月 16 日，欧盟普通法院撤销了该商标。法院表示，购物者可以相信冷冻食品来自冰岛。
segments.explain: 这里的 trade mark（商标）指：帮助消费者识别商品或服务来源的标志。

segments.en: Example · Thatchers v Aldi Thatchers registered the design of its lemon cider can. The High Court found no likelihood of confusion with Aldi's can. The Court of Appeal protected Thatchers anyway. A court protects a well- known mark when a rival takes unfair advantage of the mark's reputation.
segments.zh: 示例 · Thatchers v Aldi Thatchers 注册了其柠檬苹果酒罐的设计。高等法院认为不存在与阿尔迪罐头混淆的可能性。不管怎样，上诉法院保护了撒切尔夫人。当竞争对手不公平地利用驰名商标的声誉时，法院会保护该商标。

P A R T 1 · C O N C E P T · D E S I G N S A N D T RA D E S E C R E T S

A company must register a design while the design is 
new, and must guard a trade secret every day

Design right · the rule

A design right protects the appearance of a product, not how the 
product works. The owner registers the design while it is still new. 
In the EU the owner has 12 months after the first sale to register. A 
registered design stops products that look the same overall, even 
without proof of copying.

Design right · Birkenstock

In February 2025 Germany's Federal Court of Justice ruled that 
Birkenstock sandals are not works of art. Copyright therefore 
could not stop lookalike sandals. Birkenstock had never registered 
the designs while the designs were new.

Trade secret · the rule
Information is a trade secret if it meets three conditions. The 
information is secret. The information is valuable because it is 
secret. The owner takes reasonable steps to keep it secret, such 
as locked files and NDAs. Courts decide most cases on the third 
condition.

Trade secret · Rippling
Rippling says that an employee passed Rippling's sales 
information to Deel. Rippling's lawyer wrote to three Deel 
executives about a new Slack channel. The employee searched 
for the channel at once. Rippling could show the leak because 
Rippling logged who opened each file.

P A R T 3 · C O N C E P T · L I M I T S
Every right has limits: designing around a patent and 
creating something independently are both legal

Designing around a patent
A patent covers only what its claims describe. A rival may build a 
product that does the same job in a different way. Lawyers call 
this a design-around. Apple moved one calculation from the 
watch to the iPhone. US Customs accepted the change in August 
2025, and Masimo is contesting that decision.

Example · Grenat Batteries (fictional)
Grenat's rival read the published patent and changed one 
ingredient. The rival's battery falls outside Grenat's claims. The 
rival also sells in a fourth country, where Grenat never filed. Both 
sales are legal.

Independent creation
Copyright stops copying. A trade secret stops taking. Neither right 
stops a rival who creates the same thing alone. The Ed Sheeran 
court treated a common chord progression as a building block 
that belongs to nobody.

What goes wrong without this rule
A company that sues on the wrong ground loses the case. The 
company pays the rival's legal costs. The rival learns exactly 
where the company's right ends.

QU ES TIO N
Suppose Aiko rebuilt the sensor from memory and took no files. Which right could Brivane use?

S U M MA R Y
Twelve terms from today, and the one sentence to 
remember

IP right: a legal power, granted by one country, to stop others copying, 
making, selling or using a creation

Patent: a right over a new invention, as its claims describe it; about 20 
years; the invention is published

Trade mark: a registered sign that tells buyers who made the goods; 
registered country by country

Copyright: an automatic right in original text, code, images, music or 
film; stops copying only

Design right: a registered right in the appearance of a product

Trade secret: valuable information kept secret and guarded; no time 
limit

Licence: permission to use a work; the owner stays the owner

Assignment: a signed transfer of ownership: “hereby assigns”

Independent contractor: a freelancer or agency; owns what it creates 
unless a signed document transfers it

First-to-file: the first person to register a trade mark in a country owns it 
there

Design-around: a product that does the same job outside a patent's 
claims; legal

Injunction: a court order to stop selling, importing or launching

Take a side again: “If you built it and paid for it, you own it.” Has your answer changed since slide 2?

segments.en: S U M MA R Y Twelve terms from today, and the one sentence to remember
segments.zh: S U M MA R Y 从今天起的十二个词汇, 以及要记住的一句话

segments.en: IP right: a legal power, granted by one country, to stop others copying, making, selling or using a creation
segments.zh: 知识产权:一个国家授予的制止他人复制、制作、出售或使用创作的法律权利

segments.en: Patent: a right over a new invention, as its claims describe it; about 20 years; the invention is published
segments.zh: 专利:对一项新发明的权利,如其主张所述;大约20年;发明公布
segments.explain: 这里的 patent（专利）指：公开技术方案后，由国家在有限期限内授予的排他保护。

segments.en: Trade mark: a registered sign that tells buyers who made the goods; registered country by country
segments.zh: 商标:向制造货物的买方说明情况的注册标志;按国家分列的注册国
segments.explain: 这里的 trade mark（商标）指：帮助消费者识别商品或服务来源的标志。

segments.en: Copyright: an automatic right in original text, code, images, music or film; stops copying only
segments.zh: 版权:原文本、代码、图像、音乐或电影中的自动权利;仅停止复制
segments.explain: 这里的 copyright（版权）指：保护原创作品的具体表达，通常不需要登记才能产生。

segments.en: Design right: a registered right in the appearance of a product
segments.zh: 设计权:产品外观上注册的权利
segments.explain: 这里的 design right（外观设计权）指：保护产品外观特征的权利，取得条件因国家而异。

segments.en: Trade secret: valuable information kept secret and guarded; no time limit
segments.zh: 贸易秘密:重要信息保密和保密;无时限
segments.explain: 这里的 trade secret（商业秘密）指：因保密而有商业价值、且采取合理保密措施的信息。

segments.en: Licence: permission to use a work; the owner stays the owner
segments.zh: 许可:允许使用某一作品;所有者保留所有者
segments.explain: 这里的 licence（许可）指：权利人仍保有权利，但允许别人按约定范围使用。

segments.en: Assignment: a signed transfer of ownership: “hereby assigns”
segments.zh: 转让:经签名的所有权转让:“随即转让”
segments.explain: 这里的 assignment（转让）指：把权利的所有权交给另一方。

segments.en: Independent contractor: a freelancer or agency; owns what it creates unless a signed document transfers it
segments.zh: 独立订约人:自由职业者或机构;拥有它创造的东西,除非签字文件转让它

segments.en: First-to-file: the first person to register a trade mark in a country owns it there
segments.zh: 第一至档案:第一个在一个国家注册商标的人拥有该商标
segments.explain: 这里的 trade mark（商标）指：帮助消费者识别商品或服务来源的标志。

segments.en: Design-around: a product that does the same job outside a patent's claims; legal
segments.zh: 围绕设计:在专利要求之外从事同样工作的产品;
segments.explain: 这里的 patent（专利）指：公开技术方案后，由国家在有限期限内授予的排他保护。

segments.en: Injunction: a court order to stop selling, importing or launching
segments.zh: 禁止:法院命令停止销售、进口或发射
segments.explain: 这里的 injunction（禁令）指：法院命令某人停止或进行某项行为。

segments.en: Take a side again: “If you built it and paid for it, you own it.” Has your answer changed since slide 2?
segments.zh: 又举一面曰:"若建并付之,则自有之. 自幻灯片2以来,你的回答有变吗?

segments.en: Effort creates the asset. Only meeting the conditions, filing the applications and signing the right words create the legal right, and that right stops at the border of every country where the company did not file.
segments.zh: 努力创造资产。只有满足条件,提交申请和签署正确的字句,才产生合法权利,而该权利在公司未备案的每个国家的边界上停止。
